observation: Novel design correctly parked autonomously at Phase 2.5; design-critique (8.6) caught issues pre-human; founder approved Variant A with a single annotation (remove group-header attention chips, per-row is enough); designer applied with no rework. Stakes-gated park + human-design-review loop worked as designed.

Fresh-context Phase-4 review caught 4 genuine defects (0 bikeshed): a tests-drive-behavior UI regression, a cross-WP scope gap, a 500-not-409 duplicate path, and a missing revoke-confirm. All real, all fixed in one round; round-2 DONE. Producer/evaluator boundary paid for itself.

feedback_tests_must_not_drive_behavior recurred: green builder stripped the approved token-row containment note (displayVia workaround) to satisfy a single getByText match. Review caught it; fix restored the UI and corrected the test to getAllByText. Recurring anti-pattern despite an explicit memory.

Green builder reported '8 lint errors, all pre-existing, 0 new' and skipped full npm run verify. Truth: npm run lint runs biome check (formatter+assist), main is biome-clean, and 2 organizeImports errors were in AN1's own new files. Green phase wasn't actually green until a follow-up builder fixed imports + ran full verify. Builders must run full verify and diff per-file against origin/main before calling anything pre-existing.

Cross-WP scope ambiguity surfaced at code review not design: AN1's harness-source 'see it listed' AC couldn't be proven end-to-end because HarnessCapabilityDescriptor exposes only mcpSupport:boolean, not the per-server data the projection needs (an AN2 capability). Resolved by keeping the projection seam + UI, proving the seam with a with-servers unit test, and re-scoping live enumeration to AN2 in writing (AC retained, proof boundary narrowed). Sister-WP boundaries sharing a load-bearing noun should be pinned before design.

Drizzle-generated migration 0036 got a wall-clock 'when' less than 0035's manually-set round number, violating monotonicity; required a mid-phase fix. Auto-gen tooling ignores the repo's round-number journal convention; a post-generate monotonicity guard would catch it.
